critiques.issue: E043 rebuilt the unchanged E036 commit and got a seeds 0–2 mean of 0.7497. The three builds read 0.7532, 0.7525 and 0.7497, a 0.35 pp spread. That contradicts H4.1(a)'s claim that the 3-seed mean moves <0.1 pp across rebuilds, and it breaks H4.3.1's ≤0.25 pp prediction. H4.3.1 is still marked supported at 0.75. Because rebuild noise is now as large as most effects under test, every seeds 0–2 keep and every reused cross-build baseline is suspect.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H4.3.1 refuted and rewrite H4.1(a). Then separate the two possible sources. (1) Run one built artifact twice in the same process on seeds 0–2. If the results differ, there is within-build nondeterminism, such as nondeterministic cuDNN wgrad. (2) Check whether E043's build autotuned while the profiler or another job was using the GPU, which would contaminate kernel selection. If the cause is autotune reselection, measure what E015's cudagraph/max-autotune keep (−0.9%) costs in reproducibility. Reverting it, or pinning kernel choices through a persisted autotune cache, would make builds bit-identical again (E003=E004, E010=E012).

critiques.issue: Both cite stale figures: 'passed on 1 of 2 builds', 'population ~0.754', 'pooled 20-seed 0.7547', and a 55–70% pass probability. The tip has now passed on 1 of 3 builds. The pooled figure includes seeds 3–12, which the loop itself calls biased selection seeds. The only unselected 20-seed estimate is E044 k0 on seeds 13–32, at 0.7535. Across the three builds, seeds 0–2 average 0.7518. The tip's best time of 5.31 s is a favourable draw, not a reliable pass.
critiques.suggestion: Restate the tip's population as ~0.7535 on unselected seeds and its expected seeds 0–2 mean as ~0.752, with a pass probability at or below 50%. Before any further cut, decide whether to buy margin first, for example a +0.25 epoch top-up measured on seeds 13–32.

critiques.target: H4.1(c): 'any change re-draws every seed, per-seed differences carry little information'
critiques.issue: The data contradicts this. Seed 1 is the lowest of seeds 0–2 in 10 of the 11 runs from E036 to E046, averaging ~0.750 against ~0.753 for seed 0 and ~0.755 for seed 2. It was also lowest in most of E010–E027. A persistent ~0.3–0.4 pp deficit that survives RNG-stream changes points to a component fixed per seed, most likely the weight init, which is drawn before any augmentation RNG and is identical whenever the architecture is unchanged. E021 changed group-2 width, and therefore the init, and seed 1 was not lowest there. That fits, but it is weak evidence. As a result, the seeds 0–2 mean sits about 0.15 pp below the population mean in a predictable way, not at random.
critiques.suggestion: Add the persistent seeds 0–2 offset to the H4 pass model and gate keeps on a population of at least ~0.7545–0.755. Test the init explanation offline: rerun seed 1 with only the init RNG changed. Do not exploit this by reordering RNG draws; that would be seed overfitting.

critiques.issue: The size of the bias rests on a single comparison: E036 on seeds 3–12 (0.7557) against seeds 13–22 (0.7538). The SE of that difference is about 0.12 pp, so the gap is roughly 1.5σ. Another explanation fits equally well: seeds 13–32 may simply be harder than 3–12. That would also explain why E045 and E046 read low in absolute terms. Despite this, the 0.1–0.2 pp correction is already being used to soften the refutations of E040, E041 and E042.
critiques.suggestion: Run an older commit on seeds 13–22, for example E017 or E027. Neither was chosen by a decision made on 13–22. If it also drops about 0.2 pp relative to its seeds 3–12 number, the gap is seed-set difficulty, not winner's curse, and the post-hoc discounts should be withdrawn.

critiques.issue: This number compares E040 on seeds 3–12 with E036 on seeds 13–22, which are different seed sets. Given the seed-set and per-seed effects above, the comparison is not valid. Neither the −0.28 nor the −0.09 figure means anything.
critiques.suggestion: Rerun E040 on seeds 13–32 and compare it with E036 on the same seeds before H2.3.8 is used for anything.

critiques.issue: E045 added +0.20 s (+3.8% of 5.31 s) for +0.135 pp, which is ~1.5 s/pp, not the '~0.7 s/pp' in the notebook. The logic is also inverted: for a booster, fewer seconds per pp is cheaper, so 0.7 s/pp would have beaten the dial. The real rate equals the dial, so the result says nothing either way. Separately, the dial was measured on pre-freeze bases at 0.68 s/epoch, and the slope is quoted inconsistently (0.37 in H4.2, 0.44 in the notebooks). The 'vs dial' verdicts for E041, E045 and E046 all rely on that stale slope.
critiques.suggestion: Fix the convention: cost per pp for boosters, saving per pp for cuts. Re-measure the dial on the E036 tip with a +0.25 epoch arm on seeds 13–32. Then re-rank E045 (early batch 1000), E046 (group-2 freeze) and E031 against the new dial.

critiques.issue: E044 refuted BN recalibration with a clean paired test (K=3: −0.003 pp, 9/20 positive; K=1: −0.105 pp). H1.3.6 is still marked open, and H1.3 still lists BN recomputation as untested. The finding also weakens H1.3's own suggestion that the BN-statistics mixture matters. The averaging gain comes from the weights.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H1.3.6 refuted and remove the BN-mixture caveat from H1.3. Reuse E044's design, evaluating the same trajectory before and after a change, for any post-training intervention. Of everything run in the loop, it is the only test free of trajectory noise.

critiques.issue: H6 still says no profiler trace has been run, but E043 ran one. The trace supports the first half of H6.3.1 (non-GEMM work is 31%); the second half (group 1 plus whitening ≥35%) was not measured. H2.2.4 can be settled from E043 alone: divide the analytic conv FLOPs by the ~22 ms of conv kernel time per 32 px step. E043 also puts Newton-Schulz plus the head GEMM at ~0.85 ms, about 2.5% of the step. So H1.2.3's ≥1.5% saving from cutting iterations (5→3 saves at most ~1%) is implausible, and H1.2.2's ~3% time upside is capped below 2.5%.
critiques.suggestion: Update H6. Settle H2.2.4 by calculation, with no run. Retire H1.2.3. Lower the priority of H1.2.2, since its only remaining value is clearing up the E006 confound.

critiques.issue: No accuracy-per-epoch booster has held up since E016's weight-decay cut. E022, E025, E029, E030, E032 and E044 were all null or negative, and E013/E014 were underpowered. Every keep since E016 cut per-step cost (H2) or spent margin (H4). Only one backbone, airbench96, was ever tried, and its depth, width and per-group conv counts were changed only through narrowing (E010, E021). H1's claim that sample efficiency is the main lever is no longer what the loop's own evidence shows.
critiques.suggestion: Split H1 into the settled backbone and averaging gains versus open structural levers, and lower its confidence for current decisions. If accuracy per epoch is still to be pursued, use a structural test such as a wider group 1, or depth traded for width, rather than more scalar sweeps that 10-seed runs cannot resolve.

critiques.target: Untried directions suggested by the E043 profile
critiques.issue: Fused BN/GELU and pointwise kernels take 27% of a 32 px step and are memory-bound, yet no experiment has targeted them: no GELU→ReLU swap, no removal of a residual-path BN, no cheaper activation backward. H6.4.2, which zero-pads the whitening output from Cin=24 to 32, is math-identical and cheap, but it has never run. H2.5.2 (drop group 1's third conv) and H2.6.7 (freeze at ~71%, right after the 32 px switch) are both direct follow-ups to the E028/E037 results and are also still open.
critiques.suggestion: Run H6.4.2 next. It changes no math, so only rebuild noise applies. Follow with an activation or BN-reduction test and H2.6.7, each judged on seeds 13–32 against a same-build E036 baseline.

critiques.issue: E027 was kept with a held-out mean of 0.7526, below its pre-registered gate of 0.7535. E033's gate was then lowered to 0.752 while the tip sat at 0.7526. E015 was kept despite its own '<1% → discard' rule, and E015 is the change that introduced non-reproducible builds. Gates that move after the result is known make 'supports' verdicts less trustworthy, and in E015's case the rule break created today's build lottery.

E045 and E046 are read as small differences (+0.135 and −0.14 pp, ~1.7σ) against that baseline, but the SE ignores rebuild noise, which is per-seed and unquantified at 20 seeds.

structured_output.summary: The tip, E036 at 5.31 s, is weaker than the tree claims. On the local bar it passed on only 1 of 3 builds of the same commit (0.7532, 0.7525, 0.7497). Its unselected 20-seed mean is ~0.7535, not 0.7547. Seed 1 runs persistently ~0.3–0.4 pp low across recipes, so the expected seeds 0–2 mean is ~0.752, below the bar. The rebuild spread contradicts H4.1(a) and H4.3.1, which is still marked supported. It was most likely introduced by E015's cudagraph/max-autotune keep, which also broke its own discard rule. Several conclusions rest on single ~1.5σ comparisons or invalid ones: the 0.19 pp winner's curse could be seed-set difficulty; E040's '−0.09 pp vs fresh' compares different seed sets; and E045's rate arithmetic is both wrong (1.5 s/pp, not 0.7) and inverted. All 'vs dial' rankings use a dial slope measured before the freeze changes. Bookkeeping is stale: E044 refuted H1.3.6 but it is still open, and H6 says no profile exists even though E043 ran one. E043 also caps the Muon-related levers (H1.2.2, H1.2.3) at ~1–2.5%. H1's 'main lever' claim no longer matches the evidence: every gain since E016 came from per-step cost. Untried directions with real upside: the memory-bound BN/GELU share (27%), the math-identical Cin 24→32 padding (H6.4.2), freezing just after the 32 px switch (H2.6.7), and making builds reproducible so that paired tests are exact. Before any further cut, re-measure the epoch dial on the tip with seeds 13–32 and buy margin.
